messages:
alex: Kicking off network bring-up for eu-central-1 GPU cluster (new fleet). Need routing, peering/transit, NAT/egress, and DNS delegation validated. Planning handoff to infra-op at 09:00 UTC tomorrow.

mira: Thanks. Primary goals: 1) VPC + subnets (3 AZs) 2) Transit Gateway attachments to core transit in prod account 3) NAT per-AZ or shared egress proxy 4) Route53 private zone delegation from core account. I'll post the checklist.

sam: Quick note on transit: prefer explicit static route propagation OFF during initial attach so we don't accidentally AS-path everything. Attach with propagation disabled, then push per-VPC routes once routes are reviewed.

jin: NAT strategy: NAT Gateway per AZ is simplest but expensive for heavy egress (model downloads, S3). If expected egress > few TB/month consider an egress proxy (squid/nginx) behind an ALB with stable EIP pool or use a small fleet with autoscale+elastic IPs. For allowlisted third-party services you need stable EIPs.

lia: DNS: we'll create a private hosted zone in the core account and delegate to each VPC using Route53 cross-account VPC association. For cross-account, core-account -> add VPC association with the eu-central VPC ID from the infra-account. If cross-network recursion is needed for on-prem, plan Route53 Resolver outbound endpoints.

alex: Network CIDR reminder: use 10.40.0.0/16 for cluster VPC (avoid overlap with existing 10.0/8 ranges). Subnets: /19 per AZ for node scaling. Document ENI limits for the GPU instance types (p4/p3) — need larger CIDR if ENI per node is high.

mira: Security groups: kubelet nodes need outbound to ECR S3 endpoints and control plane subnets on ports 443 + 10250 TCP. Control-plane (managed) needs API servers open from infra CIDRs only. NACLs: keep default permissive for bring-up, tighten after traffic cutover.

sam: For peering/transit: attachments will be in the infra-account. We'll accept attachments from the infra-account transit GW and add static routes to the inspection VPCs. Also tag attachments with team:eng-infra and env:staging/prod.

jin: Cost/shipping note: Transit Gateway data processing cost in eu-central is ~ $0.06/GB (estimate) and inter-AZ transit too. If we plan heavy cross-region sync of weights/state, expect bill impact. Consider model shard distribution to reduce cross-region egress.

lia: DNS validation commands (run from bastion in cluster VPC):
```
# check private hosted zone resolution
dig +short @169.254.169.253 internal-api.service.prod
# check resolver status
aws route53resolver list-resolver-endpoints --region eu-central-1
```

alex: Routing validation checklist (quick):
- IGW attached and route 0.0.0.0/0 in public subnets
- Private subnets route 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT Gateway or egress-proxy
- Route table associations correct per AZ
- No overlapping peering routes

mira: Connectivity tests to run after terraform apply (order matters):
1) EC2 metadata: `curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id`
2) S3 via VPC endpoint: `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-models --no-sign-request --region eu-central-1`
3) Outbound IP check: `curl https://ifconfig.me` (from egress host) -> confirm EIP
4) Traceroute to core infra: `traceroute core-bastion.redwood.internal`

sam: Add flow logs to the VPC with a log group prefixed `vpc-flow-eu-central` and retention 30d. That lets us debug weird routing and denied packets quickly.

oncall-bot: Runbook link added: https://confluence.redwood.internal/infra/eu-central/network-bringup - paging policy set to eng-infra on failure of route propagation during validation :rotating_light: 

jin: Rollback plan if something breaks during cutover: 1) disable propagation and remove new transit routes 2) detach new transit attachment 3) reattach previous egress (point back to core NAT) 4) restore route tables from S3-stored backup (we keep JSON copies of route tables pre-apply).

lia: Handoff checklist for ops at 09:00 UTC: owners: alex (net), mira (config), sam (security), jin (cost/egress). Steps: terraform apply -> run Mira's validation script -> confirm dig/curl results -> smoke tests for model pull/download -> flip traffic in canary mode.

alex: small terraform snippets to double-check before apply (run from infra repo):
```
# validate plan
cd infra/eu-central/network
terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=eu-central.tfvars
```

mira: Final PR checklist: ensure tags present (team, env, owner), documented CIDRs in PR, attach route table pre/post snapshots, add expected monthly egress estimate in PR description.

sam: Security quick: WAF / ALB in front of egress proxy for external model checkpoints if downloads are from untrusted registries. Also ensure IAM role for nodes limits S3 list/get to specific buckets.

alex: Scheduling note: we'll do canary with 5% of nodes in eu-central first, monitor latency/cost for 48h, then ramp. Handoff at 09:00 UTC tomorrow — I'll post the exact join link. :shipit: 

lia: I'll take post-handoff ownership for 24h on-call. If any DNS delegation fails, call me directly. :eyes:
